items.text: Virtual reality sometimes shortened as VR. <break time="0.8s" /> Immerses viewers. <break time="0.8s" /> In a simulated three dimensional environment. <break time="0.8s" /> Instead of watching a linear series of moving images. <break time="0.8s" /> On a separate and finite two dimensional screen. <break time="0.8s" /> The VR viewer wears a special headset. <break time="0.8s" /> That makes it appear as if she is surrounded. <break time="0.8s" /> By a digitally animated environment. <break time="0.8s" /> Or a space captured in 360 degrees by a specialized camera. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a movie. <break time="0.8s" /> A VR experience can be curated. <break time="0.8s" /> By technicians and artists. <break time="0.8s" /> They can provide us. <break time="0.8s" /> With engaging and spectacular things to look at. <break time="0.8s" /> But virtual reality cannot control. <break time="0.8s" /> Exactly when and how we see those things. <break time="0.8s" /> For example. <break time="0.8s" /> A movie can choose to show us. <break time="0.8s" /> A close up detail in a characters expression. <break time="0.8s" /> At a particular moment. <break time="0.8s" /> And in a precise way. <break time="0.8s" /> That conveys specific meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> And produces a particular emotional response. <break time="0.8s" /> A viewer shown the same thing. <break time="0.8s" /> As part of a VR experience. <break time="0.8s" /> Would not necessarily be close enough. <break time="0.8s" /> To see the detail. <break time="0.8s" /> And could even be looking the other way. <break time="0.8s" /> At something else. <break time="0.8s" /> At the moment that particular detail emerged.
